2. D sits third to the left of J.
3. C sits third to the right of the one who sits exactly opposite D.
4. C sits second to the left of G.
5. E sits second to the right of A, who faces the centre.
6. D sits to the immediate right of E, who faces outside.
7. B sits second to the right of K.
8. H sits third to the right of C, who faces outside.
9. A sits to the immediate left of D.
10. A sits fourth to the right of F.
11. H sits third to the right of B.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits third to the right of D?

steps: Start with clues 5, 6 and 9: together they fix A, E and D. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
Clue 2 gives 2 cases — Case 1: J third to the left of D and J faces outside; Case 2: J third to the right of D, F faces the centre and J faces the centre.
Clue 10 splits Case 1 into 2 cases — Case 1a: F fourth to the left of A and F faces the centre; Case 1b: F fourth to the right of A and F faces outside.
Clue 3 splits Case 1b into 2 cases — Case 1ba: C second to the left of D, B faces the centre and C faces outside; Case 1bb: C second to the right of D.
Clue 1 rules out Case 1bb.
Clue 8 cannot be met in Case 1a and Case 2, so they are rejected.
Clues 8, 4, 11 and 7 then place H, G, B and K.
Final arrangement, clockwise from A: A [centre], C [outside], J [outside], G [outside], H [centre], K [outside], F [outside], B [centre], E [outside], D [centre].
D faces the centre, so D's right runs anticlockwise and left runs clockwise.
Third to the right of D: E → B → F — answer **F**.
solution.shortcut: Facing the centre: right = anticlockwise. Facing outside: right = clockwise. Fix the direction first, then count seats.
solution.trap: J is third to the left — counting in the wrong direction gives this option.

Ten persons, L, M, N, P, Q, R, S, T, U and V, sit around a circular table, not necessarily in the same order. Some of them face the centre while the others face outside (away from the centre). Left and right are taken from each person's own point of view.

1. M and V face opposite directions.
2. P sits to the immediate left of U, who faces outside.
3. R and V face the same direction.
4. R sits third to the left of Q.
5. L and V face opposite directions.
6. Only three persons sit between P and T when counted from the left of P.
7. R sits fourth to the right of N.
8. M is not an immediate neighbour of S.
9. V is an immediate neighbour of L.
10. Only one person sits between T and M when counted from the right of T.
11. P sits third to the left of S.
12. T sits third to the left of V.
13. U sits to the immediate right of Q, who faces the centre.

questions.subject: reasoning
questions.prompt: Who sits exactly opposite U?

steps: Start with clues 2, 13, 4 and 7: together they fix P, U, Q, R and N. (On a round or square table, place the first person anywhere — only relative positions matter.)
Clue 6 gives 2 cases — Case 1: T fourth to the left of P, P faces the centre and R faces outside; Case 2: T fourth to the left of P, P faces outside and R faces the centre.
Clues 12, 3 and 11 then place V and S.
Clue 8 splits Case 1 into 2 cases — Case 1a: M third to the right of S, L faces the centre and M faces the centre; Case 1b: M opposite S.
Clue 9 cannot be met in Case 2, so it is rejected.
Clue 9 then places L.
Clue 10 cannot be met in Case 1b, so it is rejected.
Clues 10, 1 and 5 then place the next persons.
Final arrangement, clockwise from U: U [outside], Q [centre], S [outside], T [outside], R [outside], M [centre], V [outside], L [centre], N [centre], P [centre].
Across the table from U sits **M**.
